# Rules

<!-- generated by scripts/gen-rules-doc.mjs - run `npm run docs:rules` -->

Each rule belongs to a pillar and is worth points in `gearness doctor` (total 162, normalized to 100). A rule with no findings earns full points; one whose worst finding is `info` earns 60%, `warn` 30%, `error` 0%, unless the rule defines proportional credit. Disable a rule with `rules.disable` in harness.yaml.

## context

| Rule | Severity | Points | What it checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context/entry-exists` | error | 10 | The entry file (AGENTS.md) exists. Without it agents start every task blind. |
| `context/entry-size` | warn | 6 | The entry file stays short (lines and approximate tokens). It is a map that points to deeper docs, not an encyclopedia. |
| `context/docs-exist` | error | 8 | Every context document declared in harness.yaml exists. |
| `context/broken-links` | error | 8 | Relative links (inline and reference-style) and their #anchors resolve. Agents follow links literally; a dead link is a dead end. |
| `context/stale-references` | warn | 6 | File and folder paths cited in context docs (in `code`) still exist. Renamed code with stale docs sends agents to places that are gone. |
| `context/docs-referenced` | warn | 5 | Every context doc is linked from the entry file, so agents can discover it (progressive disclosure). |
| `context/placeholders` | warn | 30 | Scaffolded TODO(gearness) markers are replaced with real project knowledge. Structure without content is not a harness. |
| `context/status-fresh` | warn | 4 | The status/handoff file was updated in the last 30 days. |
| `context/workspaces` | warn | 5 | In a monorepo, every declared workspace has its own harness and is linked from the root entry file. |

## commands

| Rule | Severity | Points | What it checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commands/defined` | warn | 8 | A `test` command and at least one static check (`lint` or `typecheck`) are declared, so agents can verify their work. |
| `commands/resolvable` | error | 8 | Declared commands point to scripts/targets that exist (package.json, Makefile, justfile, Taskfile) and use the repository's package manager. |
| `commands/docs-runnable` | warn | 6 | Commands that context docs tell agents to run exist and use this repository's package manager. Agents run what docs say, literally. |
| `commands/documented` | warn | 5 | Every declared command appears in the entry file, so agents see how to verify without opening harness.yaml. |

## tooling

| Rule | Severity | Points | What it checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tooling/adapters-in-sync` | error | 8 | Agent-specific instruction files (CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules, Copilot instructions) match the entry file. |

## safety

| Rule | Severity | Points | What it checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `safety/no-secrets` | error | 10 | Context files contain no credentials. Everything in them is sent to model providers. |

## feedback

| Rule | Severity | Points | What it checks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `feedback/ci-gate` | warn | 8 | CI runs the project's checks or the harness gate on every change, so agent output is verified mechanically. |
| `feedback/ratchet-valid` | error | 6 | Each ratchet entry points to an artifact that exists, so learned lessons cannot silently disappear. |
| `feedback/ratchet-active` | info | 4 | The team records agent failures as durable fixes (at least one ratchet entry). |
| `feedback/agent-loop` | info | 5 | Harness checks run while the agent works (Claude Code hook) or before each commit (git hook), not only in CI. |
| `feedback/evals-defined` | info | 4 | Eval tasks exist, so the team can measure whether harness changes actually help agents (`gearness eval`). |
